digest.component_or_area: completion verifier context assembly and recovery
propositions: Completion verifier currently discovers files agentively via repeated read_file/search_files tool calls (84-158 requests per run), with 67-82% of fetches covered by already-declared file_impact causing redundant round-trips and latency overhead.

Prefetch mechanism preloads bounded file_impact contents and referencing-commit diffs into the verifier context as a labelled byte-stable section, served once via automatic message-tail prefix cache on primary and cache_prefix on batched recovery successors.

Close gate (graph=False) prefetches only closing ticket's own file_impact; deep-review gate (graph=True) prefetches subtree-union ranked by descendant frequency, with per-file skeleton-compression and 30k-token aggregate budget enforced via fit_within_ceiling.

Prefetch is opt-in to assemble_context (default None), leaving generic review callers byte-identical; only completion gate passes PrefetchSpec, honoring the close gate's graph=False non-subtree contract.

Trusted anti-anchoring guidance (confirm full bodies against live tree, re-read skeleton-marked files) lives in static system-prompt prefix before volatile marker so it co-locates with prefetch data in both primary verifier and recovery successor prompts.

Live A/B validation shows >=20% request reduction on discovery-bound tickets (f6fc 56%, e6a0 30%) with equal verdict class; close-path own-file_impact coverage measured at 29-33% of baseline distinct reads, graph=True subtree coverage pinned by synthetic fixture.
